content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "The step showing at least one entry >1 always remains is justified by a plainly false general principle; the true one-line reason (a move always leaves a nonunit) is not given.", "errors": [{"description": "Invalid justification that the board never becomes all 1's. A non-increasing nonnegative integer sequence certainly can reach 0 (K does decrease during the process). The correct reason — a move on m,n>1 outputs gcd(m,n) and lcm/gcd, at least one of which exceeds 1 (if g=1 then mn>1) — or the invariant G_p>0, is not stated.", "quote": "A nonnegative integer that never increases and starts at a positive value can never reach \\(0\\); hence \\(K\\ge1\\) at every stage"}, {"description": "Minor omission: it is asserted but not argued that gcd(m,n) and lcm(m,n)/gcd(m,n) introduce no new primes; only the remark 'A prime absent initially has an all-zero exponent list and remains absent' is offered, which follows from (2) but is not spelled out.", "quote": "A prime absent initially has an all-zero exponent\nlist and remains absent."}], "notes": "Termination via lexicographic (P,K) descent and the primewise Euclidean gcd invariant are both correct and complete; only the 'M>1' step is mis-justified, a one-line repair. Extra 'falsification'/computational sections are irrelevant but harmless."}
